candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: identify adverse medication effects, evaluate medication response, reconcile medication changes, and provide accurate client teaching about expected and reportable effects.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ACE-inhibitor/ARB adverse-effect teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients switched from an ACE inhibitor to losartan that cough is less common with losartan than with lisinopril in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough, but cough can still occur and should not automatically be dismissed.

options.A: A previous ACE-inhibitor cough makes losartan contraindicated even when there was no angioedema or hypersensitivity.
options.B: Losartan is expected to cause cough at approximately the same frequency as lisinopril in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough.
options.C: Losartan prevents medication-related cough completely, so any cough after the switch must have a nonmedication cause.
options.D: Cough can still occur with losartan, but in controlled trials of patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough it occurred substantially less often with losartan than with lisinopril.

candidate.rationale: The current DailyMed/FDA losartan label reports two randomized controlled trials in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough. Cough occurred in 17% with losartan versus 69% with lisinopril in one trial and 29% versus 62% in the other; the label also notes postmarketing cases of cough with losartan, including positive rechallenges. Therefore D is correct: losartan can still be associated with cough, but cough was much less frequent than with lisinopril in these trials. A is incorrect because prior ACE-inhibitor cough alone is not a listed contraindication to losartan, B contradicts the trial data, and C falsely treats cough risk as zero.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough, losartan was associated with substantially less cough than lisinopril in controlled trials, although cough can still occur and prior ACE-inhibitor cough alone is not a losartan contraindication.
candidate.source_document_title: Losartan Potassium Tablets, for oral use
candidate.source_locator: Adverse Reactions §6.1 > Cough: two controlled trials in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough; Study 1 cough 17% losartan vs 69% lisinopril, Study 2 29% vs 62%; postmarketing cough including positive rechallenges reported. Contraindications §4 lists hypersensitivity and aliskiren coadministration in diabetes, not prior ACE-inhibitor cough alone.

candidate.stem: A client stopped lisinopril because of a persistent ACE-inhibitor cough and is starting losartan. Which teaching about cough is most accurate?
